text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager: high 5xx rate from alb-ingress-euc2c (auto-page to oncall)
Sam (oncall): seeing the page, jumping in. checking dashboard now.
Sam (oncall): p95 latency up and 5xx ratio jumped from ~1% -> 18% in last 4m. traffic concentrated in euc2c.
Ava Eng: I see spikes on envoy upstream reset counts, many 502/504 from the ingress logs.
Diego Infra: also getting a bunch of ALB 5xx logs showing "TargetResponseCode"=502 and "TargetProcessingTime" high.
Sam (oncall): any recent deploys?
Riley Eng: nobody in euc2c pushed a new ingress config in the last 24h. no deploy bot entries.
IncidentBot: DeployBot: no deploys to ingress-tracker in last 6h.
Sam (oncall): run quick health checks:
Sam (oncall): ```bash
# curl through ALB from a jump host
curl -v -H 'Host: api.redwood.internal' https://alb-euc2c.example.com/health || true
# check envoy reset stats
kubectl -n ingress get pods -l app=envoy -o wide
kubectl -n ingress logs <envoy-pod> | tail -n 200
```
Ava Eng: curl shows intermittent 502s from the alb hostname, sometimes 200. pattern: failures coincide with backend keepalive resets in logs.
Maya Ops: Checked route53: TTL for weighted record for api.euc2.internal was low (60s) but we just observed a larger-than-expected cache divergence at some edges. might be DNS drift + one AZ degraded.
Diego Infra: FYI, one ALB target group in AZ-c has several unhealthy targets (EC2 NLB sidecars) showing connection refused -> suspected host-level networking flap.
Sam (oncall): ok hypothesis: ALB sees target failures in AZ-c, starts returning 5xx while DNS still routing traffic there due to client caching and TTL drift -> cross-region retries hit edge envoys with reset.
Riley Eng: can we fail traffic off the affected AZ quickly?
Diego Infra: propose: 1) set target group to draining for AZ-c, 2) weight-shift in route53 for api weighted policy (shift 0->100 away from euc2c), 3) increase ALB idle_timeout to reduce conn churn temporarily.
Sam (oncall): do we have runbook steps for weighted dns shift?
Maya Ops: yes (runbook snippet):
Maya Ops: ```
# Route53 weighted shift (console quick steps)
1. Open hosted zone example.internal
2. Find A record api.euc2.internal (weighted)
3. Set weight for euc2c endpoint to 0, increase euc2a/euc2b to absorb traffic
4. Save and note change id
```
Ava Eng: I'll start the ALB target deregistration in AZ-c now. tagging logs.
Sam (oncall): I'm doing the route53 change now, will post change id and time.
Sam (oncall): route53 change submitted: changeId Z3KX-12345 (weight euc2c -> 0).
CS Bot: Notifying CS: customers with VIP prefix apac-*, eu-* may see intermittent 502s. internal CS thread: #cs-impact-1765439999.
Maya Ops: ALB target deregistration initiated: target group tg-euc2c-1 draining. seeing decrease in requests to that AZ already.
Riley Eng: Envoy reset counts dropping after drain starts. 5xx ratio reduced to ~4% in the last 3m. p95 latency trending down.
Sam (oncall): good. keep watching for 15m. start a gradual rollback of any client-side retries? we should avoid retry storms.
Ava Eng: adding temporary envoy config tweak to lower upstream conn reuse timeout to avoid hung sockets. pushing via canary to ingress-ns.
Diego Infra: k8s note: we also saw increased conntrack on host; kernel conntrack nearing 80%. I'm increasing net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max on affected hosts + alerting SRE for host-level cleanup.
Sam (oncall): customer impact update: impact window started ~1765439940, large customers in APAC saw 5xx spike for ~8m; estimated error budget consumption: medium. CS alerted.
Customer Success Bot: Posted update to CS channel and queued customer comms draft.
Maya Ops: route53 propagation looks completed across major resolvers, euc2c traffic reduced to <1% per global view.
Riley Eng: final check: envoy upstream resets near baseline, ALB 5xx count back to normal.
Sam (oncall): declaring mitigation in progress -> partial mitigation achieved. preparing for handoff to next on-call for follow-up and RCA.
Diego Infra: leaving a note to run degraded-host forensic: collect tcpdump from two hosts in AZ-c, snapshot ALB access logs for window.
Ava Eng: saving logs and creating short eval set to ensure model inference endpoints are not regressed.
Maya Ops: handoff to Maya Ops for post-incident RCA and customer follow-ups.
Maya Ops: taking on-call. I'll consolidate timeline, attach logs, and schedule postmortem with infra + eng-runtime.
Sam (oncall): thanks team. final status: traffic shifted away, targets drained, host conntrack increased but stabilized, ALB 5xx resolved. I'll close the pager and mark incident as mitigated.
IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated (partial) by Sam (oncall) — follow-up assigned to Maya Ops.
Maya Ops: next steps planned: root cause - host-level network flap in AZ-c causing target group instability + DNS TTL drift amplifying client routing. action items: 1) replace/repair affected hosts, 2) increase monitoring for DNS cache divergence, 3) add preflight for ALB target health threshold alerts, 4) add rate-limited retry guidance to client SDKs.
Sam (oncall): adding retrospective note: consider automating weighted-dns fallback when ALB target health crosses threshold to reduce manual ops.
Riley Eng: will prepare a small playbook for future runbook automation.
Maya Ops: I'll create incident ticket and assign action owners. Thanks all. :pray:
